title: Web Account Registration
author: Tom Fitch, Technical Services Team Member, 4D Inc.
featured_technology: Web Account Component (WAC) — built 4D component for account signup/login
4D classic Web Server / On Web Connection database method
XML-based settings/user storage outside the data file
Plain HTML/JavaScript signup and change-password forms

historical_commentary.text: This note packages a fairly complete web account registration system — signup, password change, login validation, and an SMTP-driven confirmation email — as a reusable, pre-11.x-style compiled component wired through the classic On Web Connection database method. The overall need (self-service account registration for a web app) is timeless, but the implementation is entirely built on 4D's original CGI-like classic Web Server model and stores data in flat XML files, patterns 4D has since moved well beyond with its built-in REST server, ORDA-based data model, and native JSON/session handling. A modern equivalent would use 4D's REST server with ORDA entities and session tokens rather than a custom URL-routing component and hand-rolled XML persistence, and would very likely also apply password hashing/salting practices not evident in this 2009-era approach.
related_updates: 4D's built-in REST server (4D v16+) with ORDA and session-based authentication supersedes hand-rolled On Web Connection URL routing for building account/login APIs
Modern 4D web apps typically store user data as ORDA entities/data model tables rather than flat XML settings files outside the data file
Contemporary security practice requires salted password hashing (not evident in this component) rather than storing/transmitting plain email+password pairs
